title: Region-aware sticky routing with preemptible fallback and sovereignty holdback for dedicated fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Teams running Redwood Dedicated need predictable throughput and clear sovereignty guarantees when operating across regions and multiple zones. Current placement and failover behaviors are too binary: either an entire request set is pinned to a region (blocking throughput elasticity) or it fails over across borders without sufficient controls. We need a mechanism that preserves throughput SLOs while honoring data residency constraints and giving predictable autoscaling and eviction behavior for zone and region-level disruptions.

Proposal (high level):
1) Sticky routing token: introduce a lightweight routing affinity token attached to customer requests that expresses a preferred residency scope (e.g., REGION:eu-west or ZONE:eu-west-1a) and an ordered fallback preference list. This token is used by the scheduler and API gateway to route to matching dedicated capacity pools.
2) Preemptible fallback lane: allow customers to opt into an explicit preemptible fallback lane within the same region (lower-cost, opportunistic instances) that can be used when reserved throughput is exhausted. Preemptible lanes have controlled eviction SLAs and do NOT cross data-sovereignty boundaries unless explicitly allowed.
3) Sovereignty holdback policy: for any fleet pinned to a residency constraint, implement a holdback window for cross-region failover. During incidents, requests will be drained and queued for up to a policy-configurable holdback period (default 15s) before failing over to a non-resident pool; failover to non-resident pools requires explicit tenant-level opt-in.
4) Zone-aware autoscaler with staged shrink: autoscaler will scale up aggressively within the same region, but scale-down (shrink) operations are done in staggered epochs with per-zone grace windows to avoid correlated eviction across zones. Shrink windows are informed by request affinity distribution and KV cache hotspot metrics.
5) Eviction throttling and throughput guarantees: implement eviction rate limits per-customer per-zone so dropping capacity does not create sudden throughput cliffs. Combine with throughput reservations: customers can reserve steady throughput per region which is honored by prioritizing their requests during capacity contention.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Routing complexity: adding an affinity token increases routing table cardinality. We'll mitigate by hashing affinities into a small set of residency-classes and reusing existing routing shards.
- Latency vs locality: honoring strict sovereignty may increase tail latency during partial regional degradation. We'll surface a clear SLA/behavior matrix so customers choose trade-offs (strict residency vs lower latency/high availability).
- Preemptible correctness: preemptible lane requires separate billing and session semantics; its eviction behavior must be clearly documented and observable.
- Operational cost: staged shrink and eviction throttling require additional telemetry and controller logic but reduce customer-facing incidents during maintenance.

Telemetry and observability required:
- Per-customer per-region throughput served (tokens/sec) and reservation utilization percentage
- Cross-region failover count and latency delta for failed requests
- Eviction events by zone, with root-cause tags (drain, hardware, autoscale)
- Preemptible lane eviction rate and churn metrics

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): implement affinity token and scheduler hooks behind feature flag; route a small set of internal tenants to verify metrics and routing scale (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (opt-in): enable preemptible lane and sovereignty holdback for beta customers; expose flags in console and API (4 weeks).
- Phase 2 (default behavior): enable regional sticky routing for all dedicated fleets with conservative defaults and opt-out semantics (3 weeks).
- Phase 3: graduated autoscaler shrink policy and eviction throttles; full rollout after 2-week production monitors.

Acceptance criteria (see list below) and on-call playbook steps documented in links.
updates: 2025-03-11: Draft design doc uploaded to Confluence and shared with PM/Infra; awaiting SRE feedback.
2025-03-12: PM review - asked for explicit billing model for preemptible lane; assigned to billing team for estimate.
2025-03-13: Scheduler prototype branch created (git: runtimes/affinity-token) and initial unit tests for residency-class hashing added.
2025-03-14: SRE requested additional observability for cross-region cache-warmup impact; added to telemetry list.

Next steps: finalize billing contract text with PM, add e2e test harness for simulated zone failure, coordinate beta tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Affinity token successfully propagated end-to-end (API gateway -> router -> scheduler) under feature flag in canary region.
Scheduler can map affinity tokens into residency-classes without exceeding 5% CPU increase on routing shards.
Preemptible lane exists and is billable separately; eviction events are recorded as structured logs and surfaced in console.
Sovereignty holdback prevents cross-region failover by default and honors tenant opt-in; verified with integration tests.
Autoscaler staged shrink prevents simultaneous eviction across zones in 95% of injected-failure experiments.
Telemetry dashboards created: reservation utilization, cross-region failover, eviction churn; alerts defined for >1% sudden throughput drop.
